cmds.narrate: Verrin's Glass. Rows of glasshouses catch the low sun like a field of lanterns. The air smells of pears and warm brass.

party_say.text: I've never seen children this well fed on the Line. Not once.
Every one of those glasshouses has a resonator under it. I'd know the hum anywhere.
…Hollin Ward's an hour south of here. Thought I'd never walk this road again.

ev_ch3_arrival.recap: The freight reached Verrin's Glass, a prosperous glasshouse town fed by extraction. Hollin Ward is an hour south.

then.text: The Engine hums at half its old pitch. The harvest will be smaller. It will also be ours, and only ours. Thank you.

else.text: We'll learn to farm like our grandparents did. I hope they were better at it than I am.

then.text: Travellers! Welcome to Verrin's Glass. Leda Vane, cooperative chair. You've come on a good year — every year is a good year here.
Because of the toll. Before it, one winter in three killed somebody's grandmother. Now our pears feed half the Line. I won't apologise for that.
I know what they say in the cities. Memories, stolen. We give a few old songs a season and get our children through winter. Ask any parent here what they'd trade.

party_say.text: And the people the toll takes more from than songs?

then.text: …There's always someone. I just try not to let it be us.
You've been to Hollin. Then you'll have heard. The Engine in the Vaults has been… overgrowing. Grafting itself to new roots. The glass is cracking, and the harvest's going strange.
My engineers won't go down. I'll pay well for someone who will. Whatever's wrong, fix it — please.

party_say.text: If it's grafting itself to Hollin's bell, 'fix it' might not mean what she thinks.

then.tutorial: The Vaults have two season valves. Winter freezes the pools into ice you can walk on; summer grows a vine bridge across the chasm. Enemies change with the season too.
then.title: Seasons

else.text: The Vaults are east, past the last glasshouse.

cmds.text: Grain for Hollin? At cooperative prices: six hundred crowns. We don't give charity to a town that turned down the same bell that feeds us.

choice.text: (Garran) "I'm the reason they're alone. Not them."

do.text: Hollin didn't refuse your bell. They refused mine. The Authority's. I was the one sent to change their minds.
My mother lived in Hollin before she married. I'll send the grain myself. As a neighbour.

choice.text: (Sera) "You said you try not to let it be you. Let it be no one."

do.text: You said you try not to let it be you. I'm asking you to try not to let it be anyone.
…That's an unfair thing to say to a farmer. Fine. The grain goes south. As a neighbour.

party_say.text: The Vaults are locked. Let's see Hollin first — and Leda has the key.

fallback.text: The Vaults gate is locked. Leda must have the key.

cmds.text: Freight's laid over here. I can run you back up the Line if you need.

cmds.narrate: Inside the glass: pear trees in impossible bloom, months early. Under the floor, something hums a quarter-tone flat.

party_say.text: That's the pitch from the fork. The same flat note.

cmds.text: The Pear & Pane. Fifty crowns a bed, breakfast included, pears compulsory.
Glasswright. I can make you armour that rings like a bell when you're hit. People like that, for some reason.
Cooperative market! Fair prices, if you're from here.
We've never had a bad winter. Mum says that's because of the bell. What's a bad winter like?

then.text: Curses are just medicine pointed the other way, dear. Use them kindly.

else.text: Mother Sorrel. I keep the orchard's old remedies — and the old curses, which are the same plants with worse intentions.
The extraction made my blight-charms useless; nothing gets blight anymore. But I can teach you what I know. Hexes. Rot, burn, wither. Useful against things that heal themselves.

else.tutorial: Hexweaver unlocked: poison, burn and vulnerability. Burn also cuts enemy healing by 25% — very useful against things that regenerate.
else.title: New job

then.text: Three verses. A grower here, a child in Hollin, and something written in the Vaults. Songs hide in odd places.

else.narrate: A performer in a feathered hat is playing to nobody in particular. The tune keeps stopping in the same place, as if the rest of it was cut away.

else.text: Don't mind me. I'm just playing the parts of songs that are left.
Tavi Marr. I collect what the tolls take — verses, mostly. People remember a line or two, never the whole thing. If I find enough lines, I can sing the whole song back to them.
Sometimes people cry. I count that as working.
There are three verses around here I can't reach: a grower in town, a child in Hollin, and something carved into the Vaults. Bring them to me and I'll owe you a song. Maybe more.
Pears, plums, quince, glassberry. All year round. My father couldn't grow a turnip.

cmds.text: A song? There's a bit my nan used to sing at picking time… 'Under the glass and over the frost, count what we keep and not what we lost.' That's all I've got.

cmds.narrate: You copy the verse down for Tavi.

else.text: Our bell doesn't ring. Gran says that's how we know it's ours.

cmds.text: We sing it when the bell's quiet: 'Ring for no one, ring for none, keep the season, keep the son.' I don't know what it means. It's ours though.

cmds.narrate: You copy the verse down for Tavi.
Carved into the glass wall, under years of grime: 'Every bell was a voice before it was a well. Sing it back and it will tell.'
You copy the verse down for Tavi.

cmds.text: You found them. All three. Give me a moment.

cmds.narrate: Tavi plays. The three verses fit together like broken glass that remembers being a window. Growers stop at the end of their rows. Somebody's grandmother starts to sing along, then stops, astonished, and keeps going.

cmds.text: That's the Picking Song. Verrin and Hollin used to sing it together, before the toll split them. Nobody here knew.
I don't think I can collect songs fast enough on my own. And I think you're walking toward the place they're all kept.
Take me with you? I'm useful. I'm also very good company, which is a type of useful.

cmds.tutorial: Tavi joined (optional recruit). Encore restores an ally's time gauge and grants Regen; Tavi's Cantor songs shape the whole party's tempo. Cantor is now unlocked.
cmds.title: New ally

ev_tavi_join.recap: Tavi Marr, a performer who collects songs erased by tolls, joined after the party found three lost verses.

cmds.narrate: Hollin Ward: stone cottages, a dry well, and a bell in the square that nobody has rung in three years. The people are thin and watchful.

ev_hollin_arrive.recap: The party reached Hollin Ward, a poor village whose bell has been silent for three years.

cmds.text: This is where I stopped being a warden.

Hollin voted against the toll. The Authority sent us to 'persuade' them. The order was to break the bell's housing and install a resonator by force — and if the town resisted, to treat the resistance as sedition.
I looked at the square. Old men, kids, a woman holding a ladle like a sword. I told my wardens to stand down. Half of them did.
And the other half?
Followed me out, eventually. They took my badge, and the Authority took Hollin off the trade routes. No toll, no freight. Three years of bad winters.
I saved their bell and starved their children. I still don't know if I did right.

choice.text: "You did right. They chose. You let them."

do.text: …Maybe. They chose. I'll hold onto that.

choice.text: "Maybe there wasn't a right. Just a less wrong."

do.text: That I can live with. That's most days.

ev_garran_hollin.recap: At Hollin Ward Garran revealed his order: break the village's bell by force. He refused; Hollin kept its bell and lost its trade.

then.text: You left with your badge in your hand and half a company at your back. We remember. We remember everything; that's rather the point of us.
Something has changed, though. Our bell has started to hum. It's never hummed. Verrin's Engine is reaching for it — grafting roots under the hill.
If you're going to the Vaults, tell whatever is down there that Hollin said no. It said no three years ago and it says no now.
And if you're passing back through Verrin… our stores won't last the winter. Verrin has grain. We have pride. Pride isn't very filling.
The grain came. We'll eat this winter. Thank you.

else.text: Tell the Engine Hollin said no.

cmds.narrate: Hollin's bell. Cold to the touch — and, faintly, it's humming the same flat note as the fork.

party_say.text: It's being drawn on. The Engine's reached it already.

cmds.text: We don't take Verrin pears. Too proud. I'd take a pear.

cmds.narrate: The Glasshouse Vaults: a cathedral of glass and roots beneath the orchard. Steam ghosts across a frozen-looking pool; on the far side, a chasm where a vine bridge sags.

party_say.text: Season valves. Twist one and the whole vault's climate flips. Summer grows the bridge. Winter freezes the pool.
Clever. Very theatrical. I approve.

then.narrate: You turn the valve to SUMMER. Warm air floods the vault; ice melts; the vine bridge thickens across the chasm.

else.narrate: You turn the valve to WINTER. Frost races across the glass; the pool freezes solid; the vine bridge withers.

cmds.narrate: The Engine Chamber. A resonator the size of a house, sealed in a glass dome, wrapped in grafted vines that run down into the floor — toward Hollin.

party_say.text: It heals itself through the vines. Burn it and it can't. Cut the grafts and it can't hide behind them.
And when the glass goes gold, it's about to spit pollen. Guard or stun.

cmds.narrate: The Engine slows. The grafts loosen and slide back toward the floor. Somewhere above, a field of glasshouses goes quiet.

cmds.text: I can retune it. Cut the grafts, drop the pitch back to safe — draw only from Verrin's own bell, once a season. Hollin goes free. Verrin keeps a smaller harvest.
Or we shut it down. No extraction at all. Verrin farms like everyone else again. Hollin's bell is just a bell.

party_say.text: A safe draw is still a draw. Somebody's song, every season.
Verrin's children got through eleven winters on this thing. That's not nothing either.

choice.text: Retune it (Mira): safe pitch, Verrin only

do.text: Hold the light for me. This is the part I'm good at.

do.narrate: Mira works for an hour. When she's done, the Engine hums a true note — quieter, smaller, and somehow lighter.

do.text: There. It'll take one verse a season from Verrin's own bell. Nothing from anyone else's.
Shut it down. If a town wants to trade its songs for pears, it should be able to ring its own bell and choose. Not this.

do.narrate: Mira pulls the resonator's heart. The dome dims. Above, the glasshouses will be ordinary glasshouses from now on.

ev_engine_choice.recap: The party defeated the Harvest Engine and chose whether to retune it or shut it down.

cmds.narrate: Evening. The freight waits at Verrin's platform. Mira sits on the roof of the last car, legs dangling, looking at the glasshouses.

cmds.text: Come up. The view's the only thing on this train that's free.
You were amazing down there.
I was fixing something I broke. It's easier to be amazing at that.
Rowan… when this is over. When we find your sister. What do you want to do?

do.text: Then I'll think about it for both of us for a while. I'm good at plans.

choice.text: "Deliver letters. Somewhere quiet. Maybe with you."

do.text: …Maybe with me. I'd like that. I'd like that a lot.

cmds.narrate: The freight shudders and begins to move. Behind it, the glasshouses catch the last of the light.

ev_ch3_end.recap: The freight left Verrin's Glass for the coast. Rowan and Mira talked on the roof of the last car.

party_say.text: Hollin's south. I need to go, Rowan. I need you to come with me.

fallback.text: Let's meet the cooperative chair, then head south to Hollin.

party_say.text: This town smells like a pie that won an argument.
Healthy children, every one. I keep looking for the catch.
The Vaults are east, past the last glasshouse.
They kept their bell. It cost them everything else.
Proud people. I like them. I'd also like to give them a sandwich.
Summer for the bridge, winter for the pool. The valves are by the walls.
If anyone sees words carved in the glass, tell me. Songs hide in odd places.
